itens.t: Israel’s First Post-Oct 7 Election Ends in Deadlock as Netanyahu and Eisenkot Blocs Tie
itens.r: Israel's historic election concluded with exit polls pointing to a complete deadlock between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition and rival Gadi Eisenkot's bloc. Neither camp secured the decisive majority needed to form a stable government immediately. High voter turnout reflected intense public engagement on national security and future policy directions. President Isaac Herzog will soon begin consultations to determine which candidate is best positioned to break the impasse.
itens.d:
Israel's first election since October 7 has ended in a deadlock, leaving neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot on track to secure a majority.

The political standoff highlights a sharply divided electorate following the events of October 7, with coalition talks expected to be complex.

itens.t: SK hynix Posts Record Q3 Profit on AI Chip Boom and Pledges Massive Shareholder Returns
itens.r: SK hynix reported record-breaking third-quarter earnings driven by an intense supercycle in artificial intelligence memory chips. The chipmaker also announced plans to return roughly 100 trillion won to shareholders.
itens.d:
SK hynix reported record third-quarter earnings on Wednesday, driven by booming demand for artificial intelligence memory that pushed quarterly revenue above 100 trillion won for the first time. The South Korean memory chip maker outlined plans to return about 100 trillion won to shareholders this year.

The company announced that operating profit rose 38 percent from the previous quarter to 83.33 trillion won, delivering an operating margin of nearly 80 percent. Meanwhile, total revenue increased by 32 percent to reach 104.62 trillion won.

itens.d:
Wall Street closed higher as a revival in artificial intelligence momentum lifted global markets.

The renewed enthusiasm for AI-driven stocks helped boost investor confidence across major indices.

itens.r: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro left Brazil for the United States following his father's recent electoral defeat and amid an ongoing money-laundering investigation. The US State Department confirmed that visas will be granted.
itens.d:
Flávio Bolsonaro has fled Brazil for the United States following an election defeat and the launch of a Supreme Court probe.

This development comes just one day after Brazil's Supreme Court ordered him to hand over his passports as part of an ongoing money-laundering investigation.

itens.t: North Korea’s Kim Jong Un Urges Military Combat Readiness at Company Leaders Workshop
itens.r: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un instructed military company leaders to intensify training and maximize combat readiness. State media reported he called preparedness his army's primary revolutionary task.
itens.d:
North Korean leader Kim Jong-un has urged company commanders to intensify training and sharpen combat readiness, describing it as their primary revolutionary task. State media reported that he made the remarks during a photo session at the Third Meeting of Company Leaders of the Korean People's Army.

The event was attended by high-ranking military officials, including Pak Jong-chon, Defense Minister Kim Song-gi, and the KPA Chief, emphasizing the regime's continuous focus on military preparedness.

itens.t: NASA Unveils Advanced Sunshade for Near-Earth Object Surveyor Mission
itens.r: Technicians inspected the massive 20-foot sunshade designed for NASA's upcoming Near-Earth Object Surveyor mission. The specialized hardware will protect sensitive infrared instruments from solar radiation.
itens.d:
NASA has unveiled an advanced sunshade designed for its Near-Earth Object Surveyor mission, measuring 20 feet tall and 8 feet wide at its base. Built by BAE Systems Space & Mission Systems, the large structure will keep the infrared space telescope cool while it searches for asteroids and comets.

The NEO Surveyor will target some of the hardest-to-find celestial objects, including those located in the direction of the Sun. Ground-based optical telescopes typically face significant difficulties searching this particular region of the sky.

itens.t: North Korea Deploys Self-Propelled Artillery Along Heavily Fortified Border

itens.d:
North Korea has deployed self-propelled artillery pieces along its western border with South Korea. The deployment coincides with ongoing military efforts to fortify the heavily guarded frontier.

Photos and videos captured at the Aegibong observatory in Gimpo confirmed the presence of at least three artillery pieces on the northern side of the Jogang River.

itens.r: In an unusual direct outreach, two Nordic leaders called directly on Russian President Vladimir Putin to halt the war in Ukraine. The diplomatic contact underscores continued European pressure to find a negotiated settlement.
itens.d:
Two Nordic leaders have urged Russian President Vladimir Putin to end the war in Ukraine. This represents a rare direct diplomatic contact between European leaders and Moscow.

The appeal highlights ongoing international efforts to find a diplomatic resolution to the conflict.

Anthropic has been heavily promoting its artificial intelligence models' ability to deliver scientific breakthroughs through press releases and posts. However, the company's IPO filing urges caution regarding how rapidly AI will actually lead to major discoveries.

itens.t: ‘Star Trek’ Legend and Sci-Fi Icon Walter Koenig Passes Away at Age 90
itens.r: Actor Walter Koenig, beloved worldwide for portraying Pavel Chekov in the original 'Star Trek' series, has died at 90. Tributes poured in from science fiction fans and former cast members across the globe.
itens.d:
The Star Trek community lost a beloved icon on Sunday, October 25, with the passing of Walter Koenig at his North Hollywood home at the age of 90. Best known for playing the U.S.S. Enterprise's Russian navigator Pavel Chekov, Koenig appeared on two seasons of the original series and reprised his role in the first seven Paramount films.

Born in Chicago in 1936 to Lithuanian immigrant parents, Koenig studied at the Neighborhood Playhouse School of the Theatre before landing his landmark television role. Beyond acting, he also contributed to the franchise by writing a first-season screenplay for Star Trek: The Animated Series.

itens.d:

The administration is seeking to showcase the Venezuela operation as a key achievement, particularly as the war involving Iran makes fuel affordability a central issue for voters in the upcoming midterms.

itens.t: Astronomers Discover Lava Exoplanet Equipped With Natural 'Sunshield' Reflecting Light
itens.r: Researchers analyzing the lava exoplanet TOI-561 b discovered it reflects roughly 75 percent of stellar radiation. This unusual albedo prevents the planet from entirely melting despite its scorching orbit.
itens.d:
Researchers observed a lava exoplanet named TOI-561 b for 37 hours using NASA's James Webb Space Telescope. They discovered that it reflects roughly 75% of the starlight it receives without melting, a feat made possible by a natural sunscreen of silicate mineral clouds that create a barrier against stellar radiation.

In addition to its reflective clouds, scientists found indications of a thick atmosphere protecting the planet from extreme temperatures on its illuminated side. Observations revealed that the side facing the star is actually cooler than typically expected for a rocky planet in such close orbit.

itens.t: Argentina and IMF Reach Technical Agreement Opening Path for $900 Million Disbursement
itens.r: The International Monetary Fund and Argentina agreed on a technical review that could soon unlock approximately $900 million in funds. The arrangement is designed to support ongoing economic stabilization efforts.
itens.d:
The International Monetary Fund and Argentina reached a technical agreement on Tuesday that paves the way for a disbursement of approximately $900 million. The IMF noted that Argentina's net international reserves exceeded program targets for the end of June, driven by strong foreign currency purchases by the central bank.

The agreement follows months of discussions focused on rebuilding reserves and reducing financing risks. The IMF emphasized that Argentina has made significant progress in restoring macroeconomic stability, though further efforts are needed to expand economic growth beyond energy, mining, and agriculture.

itens.t: Kim Jong Un’s Surprise Visit to Dandong Catches Chinese Border Residents Off Guard

itens.d:
Security measures surrounding North Korean leader Kim Jong Un's unannounced visit to Dandong caught local residents by surprise over the weekend. Authorities closed roads and locked down several residential compounds.

According to social media posts, the disruptions occurred after Kim crossed the newly opened New Yalu River Bridge on Saturday.

itens.t: Special Counsel Inspects Local Election Ballots in Seoul Following Past Shortages
itens.r: A special counsel team initiated a detailed inspection of ballot papers stored at a Seoul arena as part of an ongoing probe. The investigation centers on unprecedented ballot shortages during previous local elections.
itens.d:
A special counsel team in Seoul launched an inspection of 2.47 million ballot papers on Wednesday. The ballots are stored at the Olympic Park Handball Gymnasium following an unprecedented shortage during the June 3 local elections.

Investigators are examining the ballots, surveillance footage, and other materials at the vote-counting center. Protestors have previously blocked the removal of the election materials while demanding accountability and a rerun of the vote.

itens.d:
A UK government watchdog is considering launching a probe into the Home Office. The investigation would focus on the department's use of ChatGPT technology to process asylum claims.

The review comes amid growing concerns regarding the accuracy of the tools and the secrecy surrounding how they are utilized.

itens.t: Cowboy Space Unveils 'Big Iron' Rocket Initiative to Launch AI Data Center Constellation
itens.r: Cowboy Space, led by tech executive Baiju Bhatt, announced plans for a heavy-lift rocket named 'Big Iron'. The system is intended to deploy orbital infrastructure capable of powering future AI data centers.
itens.d:
Palo Alto-based startup Cowboy Space has unveiled its 'Big Iron' rocket initiative, aiming to deploy a constellation of 20,000 artificial intelligence data centers in low Earth orbit. Founded by Robinhood co-founder Baiju Bhatt, the company plans to build the satellites in-house and launch them using its own novel two-stage rocket system.

The Big Iron vehicle is designed so that its upper stage transforms directly into a data-center satellite once it reaches orbit. Powered by methalox-burning Clydesdale engines, the 282-foot stainless-steel rocket features a reusable first stage capable of landing back on a sea-based ship.

itens.t: Six North Korean Nationals Killed in Train Collision in the Russian Far East
itens.r: A train crash in Russia's Jewish Autonomous Oblast resulted in the deaths of six North Korean citizens. Local authorities have launched a formal criminal investigation into the circumstances of the collision.
itens.d:
Six North Korean nationals were killed in the Russian Far East after a train collided with their vehicle on Sunday. The accident took place in Russia's Jewish Autonomous Region.

Local authorities have launched a criminal probe into the collision, which involved seven North Korean passengers, according to the state-run RIA news agency.

itens.t: Venus Williams Suffers Sixteenth Consecutive Defeat After Opening Match Loss
itens.r: Venus Williams extended her losing streak to 16 matches following a straight-sets defeat to 18-year-old Lilli Tagger. The veteran champion continues struggling to find winning form on the professional circuit.
itens.d:
Venus Williams suffered her sixteenth consecutive defeat after losing her opening match at the Guangzhou Open in China on Tuesday. The former world number one and seven-time Grand Slam champion was defeated in straight sets by 18-year-old Austrian player Lilli Tagger.

The match lasted one hour and twelve minutes, with Tagger winning 6/2 in both sets. This event marked Williams's return to singles competition after nearly a couple of months away following her elimination from the US Open.

The milestone follows a wave of high voter turnout within Arab communities across the country.

itens.t: Astroscale Proposes Orbital 'Bodyguard' Fleet to Protect Satellites From Attacks
itens.r: Space debris removal firm Astroscale suggested repurposing its active debris-removal tech into defensive fleets. These spacecraft could act as bodyguards to protect critical satellite infrastructure from adversaries.
itens.d:
Space debris removal and satellite servicing technologies could be rapidly repurposed to create orbital bodyguard fleets, according to space clean-up company Astroscale. The firm demonstrated high-precision docking and agility during its ADRAS-J and ELSA-D missions in low Earth orbit.

Alex Godfrey, Astroscale's head of defense, stated that a protector spacecraft could be prepared for launch in under three years. This proposal comes amid rising military concerns over space control and recent close-up maneuvers by Russian spacecraft near commercial satellites.

itens.d:
Switzerland's foreign minister will travel to North Korea later this week to attend the official opening of the first dedicated Swiss political office in Pyongyang. Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis is scheduled for a two-day visit starting Thursday to meet with North Korean officials.

This diplomatic trip represents the highest-level visit by a Western official to the country in years.

itens.d:
Palmeiras reported a massive superavit of R$ 157.3 million in September, primarily driven by player sales. The most notable transfer was Allan's move to Manchester City, which was finalized for around R$ 220 million fixed, with potential bonuses pushing the total higher.

The influx of revenue significantly reduced the club's accumulated deficit for the year down to R$ 38.6 million. With additional earnings anticipated from tournament prizes such as the Copa Libertadores, Palmeiras expects to successfully balance its financial accounts by the end of the year.

itens.t: NASA’s Perseverance Rover Gathers Essential Dust Data at Ancient Martian River Valley
itens.r: NASA's Perseverance rover captured detailed panoramic imagery of Neretva Vallis, providing insights into ancient Martian water flows. Scientists are using the data to design effective dust mitigation strategies for future human crews.
itens.d:
NASA's Perseverance rover has spent over 1,645 Martian days gathering fine and ultrafine dust particles clinging to spacesuit material samples inside Jezero Crater. The data reveals that some particles are small enough to penetrate human lungs and enter the bloodstream. 

The findings, scheduled for publication in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, will help engineers design safer spacesuits and habitats for future crewed missions to Mars. Dust has posed significant exploratory challenges since the Apollo era, causing equipment wear and respiratory irritation for astronauts.

itens.t: Massive Fire at Seoul Shantytown Extinguished After Nearly 13 Hours of Emergency Operations
itens.r: Firefighters fully extinguished a major blaze that tore through the Guryong shantytown in southern Seoul. The destructive fire required a nearly 13-hour emergency response effort and left at least one person injured.
itens.d:
A massive fire that broke out at a shantytown in Seoul's Gangnam district was fully extinguished early Wednesday after nearly 13 hours of emergency operations. The blaze at Guryong Village started Tuesday afternoon, prompting 39 residents to flee and resulting in one minor leg injury.

Authorities mobilized 232 personnel and 110 pieces of equipment to contain the rapidly spreading fire among the densely packed makeshift homes. The Gangnam Ward office reported that 107 people from 77 households were affected, with temporary shelters established at a nearby school and gymnasium.
